issues.title: This Week in AI Pathology — 2026, week 32
issues.intro_html:
First issue — reviewed. Candidates are discovered automatically from arXiv, PubMed, Hugging Face, GitHub and openFDA, then selected by hand. This week: 97 candidates surfaced, 13 worth your time.

Inclusion here is not endorsement, and nothing below has been validated for clinical use. Papers are listed because they exist and look relevant — not because their claims have been checked. See the disclaimer.

sections.heading: ✅ Regulatory
sections.html:
No new pathology device clearances this week.

Both 510(k) records returned under the pathology product codes were already catalogued. That is a normal week — clearances in this space arrive a few times a year, not weekly.

<sub>Product codes watched: QPN (AI algorithms in digital pathology), SFH/SHW (prognostic algorithms), PSY (whole slide imaging systems), QKQ (viewing and management software), PZZ, OEO. See FDA-cleared entries.</sub>

sections.heading: 🩺 Most relevant to practice
sections.html:
End-to-End Clinical Validation of a Human-Supervised Large Language Model Agent for Enterprise Surgical Pathology Modern Pathology An LLM agent taken through actual clinical validation with a human in the loop, rather than benchmarked offline. The validation design is the interesting part regardless of what one thinks of the tool — see Validation, QA & Regulatory Science.

Consensus-Based Minimum Requirements for the Adoption of a Computational Pathology Algorithm for Tumor Budding JCO Clinical Cancer Informatics A consensus statement on what a laboratory should require before adopting an algorithm. This is the genre of paper the field has least of and needs most.

Multiclass diagnostic performance and error patterns of a multimodal large language model in oral histopathology Journal of Oral Biosciences Notable for reporting error patterns, not just accuracy. How a model fails matters more than how often — see Ethics, Bias & Failure Modes.

The role of artificial intelligence in thyroid cytology of indeterminate nodules Frontiers in Endocrinology Cytopathology remains thinly covered by AI work relative to its diagnostic burden.

sections.heading: 🔬 Methods and critique
sections.html:
Rethinking pathology image analysis through shuffling npj Biomedical Innovations A critique paper. Worth reading alongside the site-signature result — this field's most useful papers are often the ones testing whether a result means what it appears to.

Screening efficiency over experience: rapid target detection in the low-power field Cancer Cytopathology Human factors rather than algorithms: how pathologists actually search a slide. Relevant to anyone designing a tool meant to fit into that behaviour.

Methodological Considerations on Central Pathology Review in AI-Assisted Gastric Neoplasia · Author reply Gastroenterology A published methodological disagreement, with the reply. Reading both is more instructive than reading either.

Object detection in histology: a multi-dataset benchmark and test-time inference PLOS ONE — multi-dataset, which is the part that matters.

KongNet: a multi-headed model for nuclei detection and classification Medical Image Analysis — compare against existing nucleus models.

Risk stratification of IDH-wildtype glioblastoma from histopathology European Journal of Surgical Oncology

sections.heading: 🛠️ Code released
sections.html:
mahmoodlab/CORAL — ★55 New from the lab behind CLAM, UNI, CONCH and TITAN, all of which are catalogued. Worth watching on that track record alone; too new to catalogue until there is a paper and a stated licence.

HyeongSubKim/awesome-pathology-spatial-omics — ★3 A focused list for pathology spatial omics — deeper on that topic than our section intends to be.

sections.heading: 📌 Not included, and why
sections.html:
97 candidates were surfaced; 13 appear above. Most of the remainder were personal or coursework repositories from GitHub's recently-created feed — real work, but not yet something to recommend to a stranger.

Nothing was excluded for being critical, unfashionable, or from an unfamiliar group. If something notable is missing, say so — that is the correction this list most needs.

<sub>Assembled with the discovery pipeline, reviewed by hand. Sources: arXiv · PubMed · Hugging Face · GitHub · openFDA. Nothing here is sponsored, and no product is endorsed.</sub>
